summary: Established workstream-sharded, append-only per-agent development records and local/CI validation gates.

pointers: development-memory schema, immutability, and coverage tests

steps: Compared monolithic, per-agent, time-sharded, and workstream-sharded layouts through multi-agent read-only review.
Selected one append-only JSONL stream per Issue or independently acceptable non-Issue work item, bucketed by creation year.
Implemented schema, size, uniqueness, append-only, material-change, semantic-pointer, and branch-Issue validation.
Connected the validator to a repository-local pre-commit hook and CI range gate.

evidence.note: Validated all three agent-owned JSONL records.
34 offline tests passed; 2 explicitly gated live Profile tests were skipped.
TypeScript typecheck and production build completed successfully.

limitations: Agent identity is contributor-declared; automation cannot authenticate the named agent or discover an unreported participant.

summary: Performed a read-only review of the development-memory architecture and proposed a minimal Issue/workstream-oriented record, sharding, retrieval, and gate design without introducing a second task authority.
steps: Inspected the proposed archive schema, ownership rules, workflow, validation script, tests, repository boundaries, and Issue repair authority.
Compared single-file, time-based, and Issue/workstream-based partitioning against multi-agent write conflicts, retrieval cost, and record granularity.
Defined a minimal per-agent contribution record and recommended keeping GitHub Issues authoritative for live state.
Identified nonessential mechanisms to omit and gaps in append-only enforcement, historical parsing cost, and current hook/CI wiring.

evidence.target: development-memory architecture, record granularity, sharding, retrieval, and gate design
evidence.note: Completed the assigned read-only architecture and gate assessment and reported a bounded recommendation with explicit tradeoffs and limitations.

limitations: No repository files were modified and the recommended architecture was not implemented or execution-tested.
This record covers only the work performed by /root/memory_minimalist and does not claim the independent findings authored by other review agents.

summary: Performed a read-only adversarial review of development-memory growth, append-only integrity, record granularity, cold/hot rotation, sharding, indexing, and gate scalability.
steps: Inspected the development-memory rules, records, validator, gate tests, hook, CI workflow, package wiring, and repository state without modifying files.
Evaluated archive growth, full-scan costs, immutable-record enforcement, per-record bounds, changed-path duplication, append contention, cold/hot separation, sharding, and indexing tradeoffs.

Recommended retaining the minimal file-backed design at current scale, enforcing record-size and append-only bounds first, and introducing measured shard rotation only after explicit size, latency, or conflict thresholds; rejected premature database, committed derived-index, Bloom-filter, and compaction machinery.

evidence.note: Completed an independent read-only adversarial review and delivered evidence-backed scalability and simplification recommendations to the coordinator.
node --test tests/development-memory-gate.test.ts passed 4 tests; node scripts/check-development-memory.mjs --all reported PASS for the inspected archive.

limitations: The inspected archive was still very small, so shard thresholds remain design recommendations rather than measurements from production-scale history.
The review made no file changes and did not claim implementation or integration ownership.
